commits.message: fix(docs): a live program that fails to load leaves no terminal; a batched scroll acts on where the terminal is now (rich-docs-examples-xuu.0bc)

fix(docs): live terminal ends stale runs, cleans up on unmount, surfaces load failures (rich-docs-examples-xuu.0bc)

Addresses /code-review high on #175: a message from an ended worker no
longer touches the current run; a terminal still loading when the page is
left is disposed once made; an xterm or program load failure is shown and
retryable; an unhandled rejection ends the program like an uncaught error;
a build-time process.exit is recorded, not thrown into the program; live
blocks bundle in parallel; row height is re-measured; a <script setup> in
any fence no longer refuses the page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): live examples — a program running in an xterm under its code (rich-docs-examples-xuu.0bc)

A `ts live` block is type-checked and bundled as a program of its own and
served to its page as a lazily imported module. RichLive runs it in a live
terminal while it is on screen, from the start on each scroll-in, stopped
on scroll-out; under reduced motion it draws one still frame with a Play
button; it wears the site colour mode's terminal theme.

The embed (theme/live-terminal.ts) knows nothing of docs pages. Each run is
a Web Worker, so stopping is terminating it, timers included. Bytes and keys
cross BrowserTerminalHost; xterm loads from the one pin the demo shell now
also fills from (examples/_browser-shell/xterm.ts).

The simulated process gains stdin and exit, so the widgets page's own
NodeTerminalHost program runs unchanged in the browser. progress.md and
widgets.md are fully migrated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): the example widget — code, and the output it produces, as one card (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8fh) (#174)

* feat(docs): the example widget — code, and the output it produces, as one card (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8fh)

Every example on a migrated page is one element: VitePress's own highlighted
fence, and under it an output panel whose label strip names where the output
came from ("Output — produced by running the code above"), then the light and
dark fragments, CSS picking one per colour mode, or the marker's note. Labels
and captions are rows of the marker table beside the notes.

The fragment's font is the one thing a host can now set through its
all:initial, as the --rich-fragment-font custom property; the widget sets it to
the code font at a line height where box drawing joins. The blink keyframes are
included once through VitePress's head, from HTML_FRAGMENT_CSS. The light code
theme is one-light, so code and output share the One palette in both modes.

panel.md is migrated: its hand-drawn outputs are gone, and the narrow-widths
diagram is now an example that draws it.
